clue.text: Intrepid writer

definitions.meaning: a ... person is bold and robust, undaunted
Thomas ..., the English novelist and poet

explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means bold or tough, and Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

clue.text: Master-builder's issue

indicators.note: a builder puts things together anew, so the preceding word is reconstructed into fresh letters

explanation.surface: What a master builder produces or leaves behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master-builder' reads as one compound, but 'builder's' is the anagram signal working on 'Master'.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is an outflow, as a flow of water pours forth from a source.

clue.text: Scoffed about legal right-a put off

indicators.note: the eating word goes about, surrounding, the following pieces

parts.note: scoffed food means ate it greedily
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mocked a legal entitlement and was alienated by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mockery, but here it means eaten greedily; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off is to estrange or turn them against you.

clue.text: Panic at being made skipper

indicators.note: the letters are being made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone panics on being promoted to lead a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the leader of a ship or a sports team.

clue.text: Produced original work that's collected

explanation.surface: An author's own work that has been gathered into an anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing music is the act of creating it, and a calm, unflustered person is also described this way.

clue.text: Lack of taste and point in praise

indicators.note: the conjunction and the compass point go inside the word for praise

parts.note: to bless God is to praise Him
taken as written
N, north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A critic complains of insipidity while making a point in a speech of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or art has no flavour or character, which is the quality of being dull.

clue.text: A Spaniard caught Italians out

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out signals the word Italians is put out of order

explanation.surface: A Spanish fielder dismisses Italian batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' suggests a dismissal following 'caught', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Castile, the central Spanish region, is a Spaniard.

clue.text: Impressive gold coin

definitions.meaning: an old English gold coin worth a third of a pound

explanation.surface: A striking gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand or dignified person is stately, and the old gold coin worth 6s 8d bore this name.

clue.text: Gather about a piano

parts.note: re means about, concerning
taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: People cluster round a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest a crop is to gather it in.

clue.text: A number present a conservationist group as tenacious

parts.note: taken as written
D is 500 in Roman numerals
here means present, in attendance
NT is the National Trust, which preserves British heritage sites

explanation.surface: A count of those attending a conservation society.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sticks fast holds on, as a clinging, tenacious thing does.

clue.text: Run through with former coppers close behind

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
P stands for pence, small copper coins
a close is an end or conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone stabbed through, with old policemen close on their heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here it means pennies, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through money is to use it up, to spend it all.

clue.text: The woman in a harem may well feel restricted

indicators.note: the name sits in the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A girl in a harem probably feels confined.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so any particular woman, like Jane Austen's heroine.

clue.text: Having a single medico go round quietly to make notes can be very effective

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the doctor's abbreviation goes round, enclosing, the soft letter

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to sing is to produce musical notes

explanation.surface: A doctor who goes on quiet rounds and writes notes can be very effective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make notes' suggests writing, but means singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impressive in presence or effect commands attention, as a grand, striking thing does.

clue.text: Control power or strengthen?

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
force means power or might

explanation.surface: A question of whether to restrain power or bolster it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster something is to make it stronger or more robust.

clue.text: Erica's man-heart-broken

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: broken means the word heart is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Erica's boyfriend is heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erica's' reads as a girl's possessive, but Erica is the botanical genus name and 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus of heaths, the low flowering shrubs of moorland.

clue.text: Generate rebellion in the adolescent

indicators.note: rebellion means the letters of Generate rise up and are reordered

explanation.surface: Youthful rebellion is generated in a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone between thirteen and nineteen years old is a young, adolescent person.

clue.text: Most imaginative and most satisfactory housing for the aged

indicators.note: housing means the word for finest encloses the word for aged

parts.note: best means finest, most satisfactory
old means aged

explanation.surface: The most inventive and successful care home for the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing for the aged' paints a care home; 'housing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring, adventurous thinking is the boldest, the most daring and imaginative.

clue.text: Not at all bright, so extra-shy

parts.note: over means extra, left over
to shy is to throw, as is to cast

explanation.surface: Someone dim and therefore excessively timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like timid, but means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky clouded over is dull, gloomy and lacking sunlight.

clue.text: Man on the board getting a drink

definitions.meaning: a piece in the board game ... (checkers)

explanation.surface: A board director who takes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; its pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkers piece in British usage, and a single gulp or swallow of liquid.

clue.text: Prior's arrangement of tenor air

indicators.note: an arrangement of music reorders the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A monastery prior's arrangement of an air for tenor voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monk; its sense is earlier, and 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier or front-facing: something placed before another in time or position.

clue.text: A piece-just a little piece — of white muslin

indicators.note: only a small part of the words of white muslin is taken

explanation.surface: Describing a scrap of white muslin fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece, an individual article or entry in a list.

clue.text: Midshipman who was by no means hard?

definitions.meaning: Mr Midshipman ..., the hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 naval novel

explanation.surface: A naval cadet who was not at all tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is a classic English seafaring novel by Frederick Marryat.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Marryat's novel, and simple or effortless.

clue.text: Top decoration presented in a case

indicators.note: the decoration's letters are presented inside the word for a case

parts.note: a suit is a legal case, a lawsuit
MM is the Military Medal, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: A top ornament displayed in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a box, but means a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of a mountain is its top.

clue.text: Heartless, firm, and revolutionary

parts.note: Co, company, is a firm
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A cruel, steadfast and radical person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' suggests cruelty, but means with the central part taken out, as an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple with its central part removed has lost its middle.

clue.text: Young server about to return the soup

indicators.note: the young server's word goes about, around, the turned word

parts.note: a page is a boy servant

indicators.note: return means the word to is turned back

explanation.surface: A boy waiter about to bring the soup back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the little word 'to' before the page boy wraps around it; 'about' is the container signal, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is the French word for a thick vegetable broth.

clue.text: A French general would find this odd

parts.note: un is French for a
common means general, widespread

explanation.surface: A French general would find this strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an army officer, but means widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare or unusual is out of the ordinary, odd.

clue.text: Though stony, gets notice about credit

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective while the answer is a noun, loose stones on a slope

indicators.note: the noticing word goes about, around, the credit abbreviation

parts.note: to see is to notice
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Someone stony-faced still gets a notice about their credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though stony' is a loose definition: scree is stony debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the loose rubble of broken rock fragments at a mountain's foot.

clue.text: Beats playing chess-accepts a drink

indicators.note: the scrambled letters of chess accept, take in, the drink
playing signals the letters of chess are moved around

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes opponents at chess while accepting a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' makes CHSES from chess; ASTI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish or thrash someone is to beat or reprimand them severely.
